mutants.description: The millisecond tick is taken when the prescaler starts a period (count 0) and not when it reaches terminal count
mutants.reason: After rst_n is released, timestamp_ms goes to 1 on the first clock instead of after PRESCALE_VAL clocks, so every later increment comes PRESCALE_VAL-1 clocks early compared with the prescaler wrap.

mutants.description: The millisecond counter saturates at all-ones and does not wrap at 2**TIMESTAMP_W as the header requires
mutants.reason: When the timestamp is run long enough to reach all-ones (reachable with the reduced TIMESTAMP_W used in simulation), timestamp_ms stays at all-ones and does not wrap to 0 on the next tick.

mutants.description: The prescaler reloads to 1 on terminal count, as if it counted 1..N, so every period after the first is one clock short
mutants.reason: The first millisecond tick still comes PRESCALE_VAL clocks after reset, but every later timestamp_ms increment comes PRESCALE_VAL-1 clocks after the one before it, so the timestamp runs fast.
